Q: Testers unable to install app via aab link but can install apk A:

This is very unlikely related to compileSdk, targetSdk, or Flutter version.

If the APK installs manually but the Play internal testing link shows:

“This app isn’t available for your device because it was made for an older version of Android.”

then this is almost always Google Play device filtering, not SDK mismatch.

Play does additional filtering based on:

  • ABI (CPU architecture)
  • Device catalog exclusions
  • Play Protect certification

To find the exact reason:

  1. Open Play Console
  2. Go to Release → App bundle explorer
  3. Open your AAB
  4. Click Device catalog
  5. Search for one of the affected device models
  6. Check the exclusion reason

If the APK installs but Play link doesn’t, minSdkVersion is not the issue.
The Device Catalog will show the real cause.

Q: How to bold SPECIFIC TEXTS using "TEXTJOIN" or "CONCAT" formula A:

I understand that the idea is that texts that come from cells are displayed in bold, and texts that are typed directly (as constants) are written in regular font. If so, you can use such a solution, for example.
Define the ConcatBold UDF function, which will mark the places where the font is to be changed with some codes, e.g. and .
Enter the FormattedText macro that will apply the formatting to the cell.
Define a Worksheet_Change event macro that will run the FormattedText procedure if the changed cell calls the ConcatBold function.
Because such a cell cannot contain formula and rich text at the same time, the formula is temporarily moved to the comment.
If you need to edit the formula, double-click on the cell, then the formula will be placed in the cell again. This is the responsibility of the Worksheet_BeforeDoubleClick event.

In the standard module, please enter the code:

Function ConcatBold(ParamArray words())
    Dim txt As String, item As Variant
    For Each item In words()
        If TypeOf item Is Range Then
            txt = txt & "<b>" & WorksheetFunction.Concat(item.Value) & "</b>"
        Else
            txt = txt & item
        End If
    Next item
    ConcatBold = txt
End Function


Sub FormattedText(dest As Range, txt As String)
    Dim ftxt As String, i As Long, j As Long, k As Long
    ftxt = Replace(txt, "<b>", vbNullString)
    dest.Value = Replace(ftxt, "</b>", vbNullString)
    dest.Font.Bold = False
    i = 1    ' chars in txt
    Do
        j = InStr(i, txt, "<b>")
        If j > 0 Then
            txt = Replace(txt, "<b>", vbNullString, , 1)
            k = InStr(j, txt, "</b>")
            dest.Characters(j, k - j).Font.Bold = True
            txt = Replace(txt, "</b>", vbNullString, , 1)
            i = k
        End If
    Loop Until j = 0
End Sub

In the worksheet module:

Private Sub Worksheet_BeforeDoubleClick(ByVal Target As Range, Cancel As Boolean)
    If Target.Comment Is Nothing Then Exit Sub
    If Target.Comment.Text <> vbNullString Then
        Application.EnableEvents = False
        Target.Formula2 = Target.Comment.Text  'use Formula in older versions
        Target.Comment.Delete
        Application.EnableEvents = True
    End If
    Cancel = True
End Sub


Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
    If Target.CountLarge > 1 Then Exit Sub
    Application.EnableEvents = False
    If Target.Formula Like "=ConcatBold*" Then
        Target.AddComment Target.Formula2  ' use Formula in older versions
        Target.Comment.Visible = False
        FormattedText Target, Target.Value
    End If
    Application.EnableEvents = True
End Sub

Use the proper separators for your language version (commas in English version).

Q: Exporting an array in bash script A:

I saw a lot of unclear ideas and a lot of text. But I couldn't find an elegant solution.
(Perhaps due to the many replies my post will not be seen.)
1. Environment variables are only visible to child scripts (which are launched from the current script). But child scripts cannot affect parent environment variables in any way.
2. In order for independent scripts to exchange data, a clipboard file is needed.
3. the best import is through the declare and source directives

To write an array to an environment variable
use

export MY_ARR="$(declare -p my_arr)"

To import it into the script


 source <(echo -e "${MY_ARR}")

To exchange variables between scripts
(Code as an example. May need some modification)

UPDATE:(In the previous edition there was a solution through descriptors. But this solution complicates the code due to the inability to control the descriptor pointer. In the new edition, the example is simplified and a specific file is specified as the clipboard)

./share_space.sh

#!/bin/bash
script_share_space_path=$(dirname $(readlink -f "$0"))
_byffer_path="$script_share_space_path/buffer"
touch "$_byffer_path"

exportVar(){
    declare -p "$@" >"$_byffer_path"
}

importVar(){ 
    source <(cat "$_byffer_path"|sed 's/^declare -- /declare -g /')  
}

./my_lib.sh

source "./share_space.sh"
otherLib(){
    exportVar "var_1" "var_2"
    "./otherLib.sh" $@ 
    importVar
}
otherLib

./otherLib.sh

source "./share_space.sh"
importVar
#... code
exportVar "var_1"

The idea is simple:
1 Before calling a child script, you must export the variables for that script and import the variables by the child script.
2. In a child script, you need to import the variables of the parent script before executing. After the child script completes, export the child script variables.
3. Previous buffer data will be erased with each export(write) attempt. Therefore, you must always follow the previous 2 rules, and then there will be no problems with nesting or sequence of calls.

4.The idea comes down to calling scripts sequentially. For parallel execution of scripts (when 2 scripts are launched in parallel), the idea needs to be implemented via "mkfifo"

All rules boil down to the following:
what is transmitted to the recipient must be read at the earliest opportunity. Otherwise there will be uncertainty

Q: Deprecate only a specific overload A:

I have found one combination of annotation that works for me (tried on python3.11).

from typing import overload
from typing_extensions import deprecated

@deprecated("prefer the str-version")
@overload
def double(x: int) -> int: ...

...

The IDE misleadingly tells me the function is deprecated, but it shows my custom message right below it, so this is no major problem.
